summary: Sam Eggleston's Sporting News explainer describes totals (over/under) betting, where bettors wager on whether the combined score of a game will be over or under a bookmaker's line. It covers how odds work, why lines move, the three outcomes (win, loss, push), and worked examples across NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, soccer, MMA, tennis and golf. A FAQ addresses overtime, line changes and reading odds like -110.
one_line: A beginner's guide to over/under totals betting, covering how lines, odds, line movement and push outcomes work, with examples across eight sports.
key_facts: A totals (over/under) bet is a wager on the combined score of both teams, not on the winner or margin.
Bookmakers set a predicted total; bettors choose whether the actual combined score will be over or under it.
With an NBA total of 210.5, the over wins at 211 or more and the under wins at 210 or less.
Totals odds typically range from -105 to -120, reflecting a roughly even chance either way.
Totals lines move due to betting activity, injury updates, weather conditions, and other news like strategy changes or recent performances.
A push occurs when the combined score equals the total exactly, and the wager is refunded.
Most sportsbooks use half-points, such as 200.5 instead of 200, to avoid pushes.
In the NFL example, Dallas Cowboys 28 and Philadelphia Eagles 24 totaled 52 against a line of 47.5, so the over won.
In the NHL example, the Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens combined for 5 goals against a 5.5 line, so the under won.
In MMA, over/under bets refer to fight duration in rounds, such as a 2.5-round line; a stoppage midway through round two counts as 1.5 rounds.
In tennis, totals are based on games or sets; set scores of 7-5, 6-7, 7-6 and 6-4 total 42 games, beating a 40.5 line.
In most sports and at most sportsbooks, overtime counts toward totals wagers, but bettors should check the specific rules.
Odds of -110 mean wagering $110 to win an additional $100.
Neither over nor under holds a universal advantage; success depends on evaluating the line and the teams.
